The primary material of a traditional candle is wax, which serves as the fuel source, typically accompanied by a wick that draws the melted wax upward to sustain the flame.

Regarding the themes in the provided text, both J.R.R. Tolkien's 'The Lord of the Rings' and C.S. Lewis's 'The Chronicles of Narnia' share the prevalent theme of good versus evil. However, they differ in their presentation of this theme. 'The Lord of the Rings' presents a complex world with a clear distinction between the forces of good and those of darkness. In contrast, 'The Chronicles of Narnia' often blurs this line, introducing characters who waver between sides, thus presenting a more nuanced view of morality.
